name: Abano
notes: Small beach north of Guincho. Initial exposure settings need observations at the actual lesson area.

name: Adraga
notes: Open Atlantic exposure, cliffs and rocks. Mid-tide weighting is an initial assumption, not a measured calibration.

name: Carcavelos
notes: South-southwest exposure. North winds are offshore; banks and crowding change which part of the beach works.

name: Cresmina
notes: Nearby Guincho conditions provide the initial reference. Local shelter and sandbanks still need calibration.

name: Guincho
notes: Exposed beach with strong local wind effects. Mid to low tide is an initial preference; sandbanks vary.

name: Magoito
notes: Exposed coast beneath cliffs. Initial wave and tide settings require local calibration.

name: Parede
notes: Point break with a rocky bottom and potentially long paddle. Initial preference is mid tide.

name: Praia Grande
notes: Exposed Atlantic beach. Mid tide is an initial preference; conditions depend on sandbanks. Northern-wind shelter varies along the beach.

name: Praia Pequena
notes: Smaller beach north of Praia Grande, with some northern-wind shelter. Observe the banks and rocks before a lesson.

name: Praia da Cornélia · Caparica
notes: Southern part of Praia da Saúde, known as Cornélia. Initial settings represent a sandy west-facing beach and need local observations.

name: Praia das Maçãs
notes: Beach at the river mouth. Sandbanks and local currents can change; initial settings need instructor observations.

name: Praia de São João · Caparica
notes: Sandy beach near the Tagus mouth. Banks, currents and shelter vary along the beach; mid-tide preference is provisional.

name: São Julião
notes: Open-coast beach at the Sintra and Mafra boundary. Initial settings need confirmation for the selected banks.

name: São Pedro do Estoril
notes: The general beach area. Choose Bico or Bafureira for a break-specific estimate. West and south-west swell preferred. WNW swell around 280–283° can still produce small rideable surf; shelter increases sharply towards 290°. Local tuning based on owner knowledge and forecast comparison, pending measured beach observations.

sources.note: São Pedro is strongly direction-dependent; useful swell around 272°, marginal near 282–283°, usually flat above 290°. Initial curve is a local observation, not a verified universal cutoff. GFS bearings are retained as supplied.
sources.title: Owner comparison with Surfline, 5 September 2026

sources.note: Owner local knowledge, 6 September 2026: WNW 280–283° around 0.9 m / 10 s can produce small rideable surf. Supplied Surfline screenshots show Tuesday 08:00 0.3–0.6 m, Poor to fair, at 283°, shortly after low tide. Forecast comparison, not a measured beach observation. Adjust only exposureByDirection and sizeCeilingCurve; retain strong shelter from 290°, each break's tide/swell/experience rules and all other settings. No date-dependent rule or forecast-input correction.
sources.title: Owner local knowledge and supplied Surfline screenshots, 6 September 2026

name: São Pedro do Estoril · Bafureira
notes: Local guidance: favours mid to high tide with higher swell. Published school guidance also identifies mid tide. Rocky bottom. West and south-west swell preferred. WNW swell around 280–283° can still produce small rideable surf; shelter increases sharply towards 290°. Local tuning based on owner knowledge and forecast comparison, pending measured beach observations.

sources.note: Bico: low tide, mid tide with bigger swell. Bafureira: mid-high tide with higher swell.
